packageRules.description: pnpm overrides are security pins, not feature upgrades. They force a transitive dep to the latest fix *within the major its consumers are written against*. A major bump jumps the override target past that major, leaving peers unsatisfied and breaking builds. Closed #1102/#1103/#1104 (and #1162/#1163/#1164 after the pins moved to pnpm-workspace.yaml) for exactly this. Patch/minor on overrides is still fine. Matched by file because the pins live in pnpm-workspace.yaml since the pnpm settings migration; the depType rule alone stopped matching there.
Same guard for pnpm.overrides if any pin ever moves back into package.json.

The docs package is a deliberate TypeScript 6 island (CLAUDE.md § Important Constraints). typedoc caps its `typescript` peer at 6.x, and on TS7 it dies inside typedoc reading 'PropertyDeclaration', taking `pnpm -F docs build:all` with it; `check:snippets` fails separately with 'ts.createProgram is not a function', since the TS7 native compiler does not expose the JS API that script uses. The rest of the workspace is on TS7 and pnpm's per-package isolation keeps the two apart. Closed #1342 for exactly this. Revisit when typedoc supports TS7 — and delete this rule then rather than widening it.

A package declared as BOTH a peerDependency and a devDependency must move in one PR. The devDep exists only to satisfy the peer locally, so bumping one and not the other leaves the package contradicting itself, and with autoInstallPeers pnpm resolves a second copy. For a type-bearing package that is fatal: two zod copies made TypeScript reject its own types (`Type '5' is not assignable to type '4'`), breaking every release job on master. That happened because the `Dev dependencies` rule above captured zod's devDependency while its peerDependency stayed in `Non-major dependencies` — two PRs, merged hours apart, skewed in between. #632 is the same failure mode for act itself. `{{{depName}}}` groups per package, so these keep their own PRs rather than piling into one.
